Standardize spelling to US English by updating focussed to focused and focussing to focusing, and add both British variants to .vscode/dictionaries/forbidden-spelling.txt so cSpell can catch them going forward.

items.content_html:
Description

Documents the impact of State Partitioning on the Web Storage API (localStorage and sessionStorage) when accessed from embedded third-party contexts (iframes).

Motivation

Historically, MDN documentation stated that localStorage is partitioned solely by document origin. In modern browsers, client-side storage is double-keyed under State Partitioning when accessed within third-party <iframe>s (keyed by both the origin of the document and the top-level site) to prevent cross-site tracking. Explicitly documenting this behavior and cross-referencing MDN's privacy documentation prevents confusion for web developers building embedded applications.

Additional details

  • Added a dedicated ### Storage partitioning subsection to files/en-us/web/api/window/localstorage/index.md.
  • Updated files/en-us/web/api/web_storage_api/index.md and files/en-us/web/api/window/sessionstorage/index.md to remove the outdated claim that localStorage is partitioned by origin only.
  • Added cross-links to MDN's State Partitioning guide across all affected pages.
  • Tested and formatted with markdownlint-cli2 and prettier.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #43255
items.title: docs(web-storage): document state partitioning in Web Storage API

items.content_html:
FF160 ships the speech recognition side of the Web Speech API on desktop, with on-device recognition (https://bugzil.la/2080908).

This reviews the speech recognition docs against the spec, BCD, and the Firefox and Chromium implementations, and fixes the problems found:

  • Broken links: available()/install() cross-links and two "on-device" demo links that pointed at the non-on-device demo
  • SpeechRecognitionAlternative.confidence and transcript named the wrong interface
  • install(): added NotAllowedError (transient activation, Permissions Policy), documented processLocally, and removed the incorrect "only takes langs" claim (also in the guide)
  • Where recognition runs: the browser chooses by default, and setting processLocally to false doesn't force a cloud service (Firefox has none)
  • A missing language pack fires an error event with service-not-allowed (per spec), not a thrown language-not-supported
  • Permissions Policy: available() resolves to unavailable and install() rejects with NotAllowedError (Chrome and Firefox agree; the spec doesn't say)
  • available(): added a download-masking note, and put the multi-language status rules in spec order
  • start() and stop() don't return results; added start()'s missing InvalidStateError cases; the result event also fires for interim results
  • Alternatives are possible matches for what the user said, not single words; grammars have no effect on recognition
  • SpeechRecognitionResultList: the continuous-mode description on the overview was backwards
  • Guide example fixes: let voices, map()/join() (not forEach()), and — DEFAULT
  • Renames SpeechGrammarList.addFromURI() to addFromUri(), matching the spec, Chromium and Firefox. This depends on mdn/browser-compat-data#31089 being released, so don't merge until then.

Related BCD: mdn/browser-compat-data#31080

Related docs work can be tracked in #46283

🤖 Generated with Claude Code
items.title: FF160 Web Speech API: speech recognition docs fixes

items.content_html:
Updates the <img> srcset reference to describe the deterministic source selection algorithm from the HTML Standard, and removes "network speed" from the list of factors in the Responsive images guide.

Motivation

The HTML Standard now defines responsive image source selection normatively (whatwg/html#13183) instead of leaving it implementation-defined. The docs still said the browser picks a source "at its discretion" based on things like bandwidth, which no longer matches the spec or what browsers actually do.

Additional details

The new srcset text describes these steps:

  1. Deduplicate candidates with the same pixel density, keeping the earliest.
  2. Sort candidates by ascending pixel density.
  3. Pick the first candidate whose density is greater than or equal to Window.devicePixelRatio, or the last one if all are lower.

It also notes that the browser may pick a higher-density candidate if its image data is already available without a network request.

  • whatwg/html#13183
  • whatwg/html#13077
  • web-platform-tests/wpt#64665

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46377
items.title: Document normative srcset image source selection
